rationale: Experiment for the sharpened investigation 0bfc2ea5a9e94316982943d306eefbf6-question-0. It reuses the harness file already in the draft, now extended with a hand-built three-node cluster made from the library's own in-memory transport, store and snapshot store so that one node's LogStore can be wrapped to return an allowed error from StoreLogs. The history staged is a legal single-cluster one: the initial leader is partitioned, keeps accepting client work into its own log (uncommitted), the remaining two voters elect a leader at a higher term and commit different entries at the same indices, then the partition heals. The control runs the identical history with a healthy store. Native local feedback on this harness in a scratch copy inside draft produced the expected divergence between the two cases, so the prediction is credible but is not treated as the conclusion; the retained execution decides. The earlier leadership-transfer harness was kept in the same file so the file remains self-contained and the first witness stays reproducible from it.

scope.description: Two subtests run the same legal history, differing only in whether the node's store fails the StoreLogs call that follows a conflicting-suffix deletion. Each case builds three voters with NewInmemTransport, NewInmemStore (wrapped by a legal fault-injecting LogStore implementing the interface), NewInmemSnapshotStore and the package MockFSM, bootstrapped with the library's BootstrapCluster and started with NewRaft. The initial leader is then isolated at the transport level, keeps two Apply calls in its own log, the other two nodes elect a leader at a higher term and commit two entries, and the partition is healed. The case records: the diverging node's cached certificate (getLastEntry), its reported LastIndex, commit and applied indexes, the wrapped store's FirstIndex/LastIndex and whether GetLog of the certificate index errors, and the store's StoreLogs attempt/delivery counters, sampled every 25 ms for 1500 ms after the heal and once more 1200 ms after the fault (if any) is removed. The leader's own certificate and store counters are recorded alongside.
assumptions: A LogStore returning an error from StoreLogs is an allowed outcome of the interface, not corruption of an acknowledged durable write; the wrapper returns such an error without touching the underlying store.

The staged history is a legal single-cluster history: the diverging node's tail entries were appended while it was partitioned and therefore uncommitted, and the majority's replacement entries are committed at a higher term.
In-memory LoopbackTransport delivers RPCs in-process without loss, so nonprogress is produced by the library's logic rather than by transport faults.
The fault is armed only on the diverging node and only after the majority has committed its replacement entries, so the failing call is the StoreLogs that follows the conflicting-suffix deletion.
excluded: No production code is modified; the wrapper implements the public LogStore interface only.
No snapshot install, restart or leader-side compaction is performed, so the question of whether those repair the state stays open in this execution.

experiment.prefix: Each case prints CA_EVENT JSON lines: truncation_before_heal (the two nodes' probes before the partition heals), truncation_after_heal (probes plus the 1500 ms sampling arrays cert_index_samples, store_last_samples, store_attempts), and truncation_after_disarm (a probe 1200 ms after the fault is removed). Probes carry cert_last_index/cert_last_term, reported_last, commit_index, applied_index, store_first/store_last, store_attempts/store_delivered and cert_entry_error.
